tongatapu.tagline: Nukuʻalofa, royal tombs and a rugged south coast on Tonga's main island
tongatapu.description: The main island of Tonga, Tongatapu is a low coral-limestone island of about 260 km2 with the capital, Nukuʻalofa, on its north shore. Visitors come for the ancient royal sites: the Haʻamonga ʻa Maui trilithon and the langi tombs of the Tuʻi Tonga kings at Muʻa. The rugged south coast adds the Mapu ʻa Vaea blowholes and the Hufangalupe land bridge. A central market and Sunday church singing show everyday Tongan culture.
whyVisit: Explore ancient royal tombs and monuments
Watch blowholes spout along the south coast
Explore sea arches and cave pools

goodToKnow.title: Sunday is a rest day
goodToKnow.detail: Almost all shops and services close on Sunday, so book Sunday food with your hotel, especially if you arrive on Saturday.

goodToKnow.title: Buses run on roadside signals
goodToKnow.detail: Buses leave from the Nukuʻalofa seafront with no posted timetable and are unreliable after about 15:30. Flag them down.

goodToKnow.title: Dress modestly
goodToKnow.detail: Dress modestly in towns and villages. Some cruise visitors have been arrested for walking around topless.

tongatapu.bestTimeBlurb: The cool, dry season from {months} suits sightseeing, with humpback whales offshore from July.

vavau.tagline: More than 50 islands of calm anchorages, coral gardens and humpback calves
vavau.description: Vavaʻu is a raised-limestone and coral archipelago about 250 km north of Tongatapu, with the harbour town of Neiafu on ʻUtu Vavaʻu. A string of islands and reefs along the eastern edge protects the waters, and humpback whales give birth here. About 500 yachts visit each winter sailing season, drawn by hidden coves and beaches. Swallows Cave and Mariner's Cave suit snorkellers and divers, Mt Talau has a short trail with harbour views, and the group is a major producer of high-quality vanilla.
whyVisit: Swim with humpback mothers and calves
Snorkel coral gardens and sea caves

goodToKnow.title: Book licensed whale operators
goodToKnow.detail: Use only licensed operators. July to October is busiest, so book tours and rooms well ahead.

goodToKnow.title: Getting to Vavaʻu
goodToKnow.detail: International flights land at Tongatapu. Lulutai Airlines flies on to Vavaʻu, and a ferry also runs.

goodToKnow.title: Carry cash on outer islands
goodToKnow.detail: Cards are not widely taken, so bring enough cash before heading out to the outer islands.

vavau.bestTimeBlurb: Swim with humpbacks in {months}, in the cooler trade-wind season that also suits sailing.

eua-island.tagline: Cliffs, caves and rainforest trails on Tonga's oldest island, south of Tongatapu
eua-island.description: ʻEua is a hilly, non-volcanic island of 87 km2, Tonga's oldest geologically, rising to 312 m. ʻEua National Park, Tonga's only forest national park, has marked trails and the Big Ovava Tree, said to be over 800 years old. Lookouts such as Lakufaʻanga Cliff and the Liʻangahuo ʻa Maui stone bridge sit along the coast, and birdwatchers look for the rare red shining parrot. The seven-minute flight from Tongatapu is one of the world's shortest commercial flights.
whyVisit: Hike rainforest trails and sea cliffs
Explore caves and natural stone bridges

goodToKnow.title: Flight or ferry
goodToKnow.detail: The short Lulutai flight from Tongatapu takes about seven minutes. The ferry from Nukuʻalofa takes 2.5 to 3 hours, so check the schedule.

goodToKnow.title: Getting around
goodToKnow.detail: Rent a car, take a taxi or use local buses. Most businesses close on Sunday, so plan meals ahead.

eua-island.bestTimeBlurb: {months} is cool and dry, the best time for hiking the cliff and forest trails.
